import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Star.Real
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.PosDef
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
open Matrix
set_option autoImplicit false
/-!
# Actual cosine-grid precision admissibility

Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1, Eq11 and Lemma4.6. The literal
cosine-grid precision is used for every full real orthogonal O, with exactly
source d>=2 and kappa>=2. The two matrix differences are positive semidefinite
in quadratic-form order, and positive definiteness is produced internally.
The source dimension binder is deliberately retained even though the scalar
cosine envelope and matrix bound proof work for every choice of angles.

The actual inverse-precision Gaussian law-density consumer is in the focused
Test and reuses the existing canonical GaussianPrecisionDensity leaf. No
calculus, known-normalizer product, moment/Krylov, algorithm/TV/cost transport
or main-lower-bound completion is asserted by this pointwise matrix result.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAdmissibility
theorem actual_precision_admissible {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
        Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    A.PosDef ∧ (A - 1).PosSemidef ∧
      (κ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) - A).PosSemidef := by
  classical
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let diagonalValue : Fin d → ℝ := fun i =>
    (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)
  let U : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := O
  let L : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := Matrix.diagonal diagonalValue
  let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := U * L * U.transpose
  change A.PosDef ∧ (A - 1).PosSemidef ∧
    (κ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) - A).PosSemidef
  have hcoef : 0 ≤ (κ - 1) / 2 := by linarith
  have hvalue (i : Fin d) : 1 ≤ diagonalValue i ∧ diagonalValue i ≤ κ := by
    have hlo := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.neg_one_le_cos (θ i)) hcoef
    have hhi := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Real.cos_le_one (θ i)) hcoef
    dsimp only [diagonalValue]
    constructor <;> nlinarith
  have hO : U * U.transpose = 1 := by
    simpa only [U] using
      (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff (n := Fin d) (R := ℝ)).mp O.property
  have hstar : U.conjTranspose = U.transpose := by
    ext i j
    simp
  have hdiaglo : Matrix.diagonal (fun i => diagonalValue i - 1) = L - 1 := by
    ext i j
    by_cases hij : i = j <;> simp [L, hij]
  have hdiaghi : Matrix.diagonal (fun i => κ - diagonalValue i) = κ • 1 - L := by
    ext i j
    by_cases hij : i = j <;>
      simp [L, hij, smul_eq_mul]
  have hlow : (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => diagonalValue i - 1)).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal (fun i => sub_nonneg.mpr (hvalue i).1)
  have hhigh : (Matrix.diagonal (fun i => κ - diagonalValue i)).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal (fun i => sub_nonneg.mpr (hvalue i).2)
  have hloweq : U * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => diagonalValue i - 1) * U.transpose =
      A - 1 := by
    dsimp only [A]
    rw [hdiaglo, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.mul_one, hO]
  have hhigheq : U * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => κ - diagonalValue i) * U.transpose =
      κ • 1 - A := by
    dsimp only [A]
    rw [hdiaghi, Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.mul_smul,
      Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.smul_mul, hO]
  have hAlo : (A - 1).PosSemidef := by
    rw [← hloweq]
    simpa only [hstar] using hlow.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same U
  have hAhi : (κ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) - A).PosSemidef := by
    rw [← hhigheq]
    simpa only [hstar] using hhigh.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same U
  have hpos := Matrix.PosDef.posSemidef_add hAlo
    (Matrix.PosDef.one : (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).PosDef)
  exact ⟨by simpa only [sub_add_cancel] using hpos, hAlo, hAhi⟩
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumAdmissibility

publication_context.statement: Every actual cosine-grid precision lies between the identity and κ times the identity and is positive definite. I_d\preceq A\preceq\kappa I_d,\qquad A\succ0. \(d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge2,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge2\). Fix any actual \(O\in O(d)\), including either determinant sign. The assertion holds pointwise; no Haar law or private-randomness premise is needed. For source indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(\lambda_i=(\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2\), and \(A=O\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)O^\top\). Lean uses zero-based \(i.\mathrm{val}+1/2\); the focused Test proves that index alignment. Matrix order is quadratic-form order: \(I_d\preceq A\) means \(A-I_d\) is positive semidefinite, and \(A\preceq\kappa I_d\) means \(\kappa I_d-A\) is positive semidefinite. This does not require every entry to be nonnegative. The finite-support definition covers all real coordinate vectors. Positive definiteness, symmetry, scalar interval bounds and both orthogonality identities are produced or obtained from the source orthogonal-group input; none is a new public hypothesis. The dimension premise is retained exactly even though the cosine envelope works for every angle. The actual Gaussian consumer is \(\pi_A=N(0,A^{-1})\) on Euclidean space with Lebesgue reference volume and real exponent \(d/2\), including odd dimensions. Its positive precision comes from this producer. Known-normalizer products independent of \(O\), full Appendix C.4 calculus/minimizer, moments/Krylov, adaptive/precision/cost/TV adapters and both complete main bounds remain separate.

steps.title: Bound each actual diagonal value
steps.text: Since κ≥2, its cosine coefficient is nonnegative. Multiply the standard bounds −1≤cos θᵢ≤1 by that coefficient to obtain the exact source interval, without a spectral-window premise.
steps.lean: hcoef is derived from hκ; hvalue consumes Real.neg_one_le_cos, Real.cos_le_one and exact real arithmetic.

steps.title: Form the two positive diagonal differences
steps.text: Use the actual scalar differences as diagonal entries. Nonnegative diagonal entries make these two actual diagonal matrices positive semidefinite, including their symmetry.
steps.lean: hdiaglo/hdiaghi prove the actual matrix identities entrywise; hlow/hhigh call the canonical PosSemidef.diagonal fact on the proved scalar bounds.

steps.title: Conjugate through the actual rotation
steps.text: Use OOᵀ=I from full real orthogonality. Distributing the actual products identifies the two differences with conjugates of the proved positive diagonal matrices. Positive semidefiniteness is preserved under this actual conjugation.
steps.lean: hO, hstar and the distribution identities hloweq/hhigheq feed hAlo/hAhi via PosSemidef.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same.

steps.title: Produce strict positivity
steps.text: Add the positive identity matrix to the first semidefinite difference. Every nonzero vector has strictly positive identity quadratic form, so the actual precision is positive definite. This is an output consequence.
steps.lean: hpos combines the canonical PosDef.one and PosDef.posSemidef_add with hAlo, then cancels the subtracted identity.

steps.title: Consume the actual precision in its Gaussian density
steps.text: The focused Test applies the producer to this same literal A and passes its positive-definite output to the existing canonical positive-precision Gaussian density theorem. The actual inverse-covariance Gaussian equals the actual quadratic-potential density, with no supplied positivity or correct-density hypothesis.
steps.lean: Tests.GaussianComplexityFixedSpectrumAdmissibility obtains hA from actual_precision_admissible and calls GaussianPrecisionDensity.multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity_of_posDef A hA. This existing shared node is a consumer dependency, not a producer proof parent.
